/-!
# Erdős Problem 275

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/275](https://www.erdosproblems.com/275)
- [CrVE70] R.B. Crittenden and C.L. Vanden Eynden, *Any n arithmetic progressions covering the first
  2^n integers cover all integers*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (1970), 475-481.
-/

open Set

namespace Erdos275

/--
If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not
necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.

This is best possible as the system $2^{i-1}\pmod{2^i}$ shows. This was proved independently by
Selfridge and Crittenden and Vanden Eynden [CrVE70].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos275.lean"]
theorem erdos_275 (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) (n : Fin r → ℕ)
    (H : ∃ k : ℤ, ∀ x ∈ Ico k (k + 2 ^ r), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]) (x : ℤ) :
    ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD n i] := by
  sorry

end Erdos275

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement permits zero moduli, which Int.ModEq interprets as singleton classes, whereas ordinary arithmetic progressions use positive moduli. It also uses an arbitrary translated block rather than the first 2^r integers appearing in CrVE70's title.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restriction to positive moduli is immediate. Conversely, assume the positive-modulus theorem and fix a target integer x. Replace every zero modulus n_i by |a_i−x|+1, leaving positive moduli unchanged. Each original singleton is contained in its replacement class, so the covered block remains covered. Applying the positive-modulus theorem covers x. If its covering class was replaced, divisibility of a_i−x by |a_i−x|+1 forces x=a_i, so the original singleton also covers x. Thus the unrestricted conclusion follows for every x. Translation by 1−k identifies the integer interval [k,k+2^r) with {1,…,2^r}. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted problem theorem; their axiom reports contain no sorryAx.
